line: Jung's statements on the Kore: the maiden of the Demeter myth, her appearance as an unknown young girl, and her difference from the anima.

sections.title: The maiden and the mother
sections.line: CW9i ¶156 and ¶306–316: Kore with Demeter, and the image of the young girl in dreams.

quotes.quote: Mythology offers many variations of the mother archetype, as for instance the mother who reappears as the maiden in the myth of Demeter and Kore; or the mother who is also the beloved, as in the Cybele-Attis myth.
At this level the mother is both old and young, Demeter and Persephone, and the son is spouse and sleeping suckling rolled into one.
In fact, the psychology of the Demeter cult bears all the features of a matriarchal order of society, where the man is an indispensable but on the whole disturbing factor.

sections.title: Kore and the anima
sections.line: CW9i ¶356: how the Kore and the anima are told apart.

quotes.quote: All that remains for me now is to describe the Kore as observable in man, the anima.
Although the anima can, as we have said, experience herself in Demeter-Kore, she is yet of a wholly different nature.
